question: In which of following Yajnas was a horse let loose to wander freely and guarded by the raja’s men in ancient India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashvamedha Yajna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Ashvamedha yajna was a ritual sacrifice of a horse performed by ancient Indian kings to demonstrate their imperial sovereignty. 
 
• The horse was a symbol of power and virility, and its sacrifice was seen as a way of asserting the king's dominance over his enemies and vassals.
 
• The Ashvamedha yajna was a complex and costly ritual, and it was only performed by the most powerful kings. 
 
• The ceremony involved a number of different steps, including the selection of the horse, its journey through the kingdom, and the final sacrifice.
 
• The horse was chosen from the king's own stables, and it was decorated with gold and jewels. 
 
• The horse was then released to wander for a year, accompanied by a group of warriors. 
 
• During its journey, the horse was not allowed to be harmed or captured. 
 
• If any enemy tried to stop the horse, the warriors were required to fight them.
 
• After one year, the horse was returned to the king's capital. 
 
• The Ashvamedha yajna was a powerful symbol of the king's power and authority. 
 
• It was a way of demonstrating to the kingdom and to the world that the king was a powerful ruler who was not to be challenged. 
 
• The Ashvamedha yajna was also a way of ensuring the king's prosperity and success.
 
• The Ashvamedha yajna was a controversial ritual, and it was eventually abandoned by most Hindu kings. 
 
• 
 
However, it remains an important symbol in Hindu culture, and it is still sometimes performed today.
